text.p: These are the highlights of the main stories in the Bosnian press on Friday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bosnia must open its door wide to foreign capital, said Haris Silajdzic, co-chairman of the Council of Ministers, following visit by Bosnian delegation to Malaysia.
- Deputy High Representative Gerd Wagner said on Thursday that early parliamentary elections are the "only way" to break the current political impasse in Bosnia's Serb entity.

- Kris Janowski, spokesman for the office of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees in Sarajevo, says about 500 Moslem refugees are due to return this weekend to the Jajce area, from where they have been recently expelled.

- Serge Robert, the central bank governor, says he expects the new currency, the convertible mark, to become the dominate currency which will be used more than both the Yugoslav dinar and the Croatian kuna in Serb or Croat areas.

- The Moslem ruling Party of Democratic Action (SDA) denies that a division of territories was discussed during the recent meeting between Bosnia's collective presidency chairman Alija Izetbegovic and Croatian President Franjo Tudjman.
- Some Bosnian media reported that the two leaders were suggesting that the Serb-controlled town of Banja Luka should become part of the country's Moslem-Croat federation.
- The average salary in June in the Moslem-Croat federation was 257 German marks ($142), Hasan Zolic, director of the the state statistics agency, said. --Sarajevo Newsroom, +387-71-663-864
